has no figures, no projection and no running timer. `active` is false
while its client or its project is archived: it is read, but never

BillingEntryResponse.description:

CarryOver.description: What becomes of the vacation days left at the end of a year.

ClientBillingResponse.description:

ClientUpdateRequest.description:
Request body for replacing a client: the same keys, and

ClientWriteRequest.description:
Request body for adding a client: the domain's fields, every key

CompanyHoliday.description:
A day off the employer gives that the region's calendar does not —
Christmas Eve, a bridge day, a company day. A whole day, on one date.
CompanyHoliday.title: CompanyHoliday

Contract.description:
A day job's terms as they changed over time, plus what frames them.

`terms` is the history — part-time, then 80%, then full-time — kept in
order of `effective_from` with no two starting on the same day, because
the day decides which term applies. The region names the employer's
public holidays: `holiday_subdivision` only means something inside a
`holiday_country`. Both must be codes the holidays library knows, but
that is checked where a contract is written (`ProjectService`), not
here: this model is re-validated on every read, and the set of codes the
library knows moves with its version — a code it stops recognising must
make one contract un-editable, not every project of the user unreadable.
`opening_balance_hours` is what was banked (or owed) before Beats started
counting; `ended_on` freezes the balance from that day on.

Where the employer's days off differ from the region's, two lists say
how: `company_holidays` adds days, `holidays_not_given` takes region
holidays away (`domain/holidays.contract_calendar` combines the three).
A removal that matches no region holiday — or is kept while there is no
region — does nothing; a company day on a removed date wins. Each list's
only rule is its own (no date twice), and no rule may ever tie either
list to another field or to the other list: an incoming contract that
leaves a list out keeps the stored one (`keep_unsent_contract_fields`),
merged without re-validating, which is safe only while every rule on
these lists is per-list. A cross-field rule would need that merge to
re-validate and answer a 422 — otherwise a merged contract could fail
the next read, and every project of the user with it.

`vacation` is the leave the job gives (`VacationEntitlement`), None when
nothing is tracked. It is kept when left out the same way, and so has no
rule here tying it to the terms or `ended_on`: that its opening falls
inside the contract's dates is checked after the merge, on the write.
Contract.title: Contract

ContractDay.description:
One day of a contract week: what it owed, what was worked, and why it
owed less if it did.
ContractDay.title: ContractDay

ContractTerm.description:
One stretch of a contract, from `effective_from` until the next term takes over.

A time-based term (full_time / part_time) owes `full_time_hours × percentage`
a week — a percentage needs its basis, since 80% of 42 is not 80% of 40. A
custom term states `weekly_hours` outright. An objective term owes nothing
and carries no numbers at all. Hence the rules:

- `percentage` lies in (0, 1]; a full_time term is 1 — filled in when
  omitted, rejected when it says otherwise — and a part_time term is
  less than 1, or it would be full-time under another name.
- `weekly_hours` is required for custom and must be left out for the
  time-based types, where it is derived (`hours_per_week`).
- `full_time_hours` and `percentage` belong to the time-based types only.

`effective_from` may be any day of the week: a contract that changes on a
Wednesday charges Monday and Tuesday at the old rate.
ContractTerm.title: ContractTerm

ContractWeek.description:
A day job's week against its contract, plus the running balance.

Typed because it crosses the wire (see `ProjectBreakdownEntry`).
`expected` and `remaining` are None when the contract owes nothing by
nature that week — no weekday has a time-based term in force — as
distinct from 0, which is a week the contract owed nothing by
circumstance (every weekday a holiday, or after `ended_on`). `balance`
is None on the same rule for today. `remaining` goes negative once the
week is over its expectation. `worked` is every hour on the project that
week; `remaining` subtracts only the hours the balance counts — inside
the contract's dates, under a term that owes hours — so the two differ
on a week it starts or ends, or a term that owes nothing begins or ends.
Each figure is rounded on its own, so `worked + remaining` can miss
`expected` by a hundredth.
ContractWeek.title: ContractWeek

CreateBeatRequest.description:

server-side from the daemon's flow signals (see BeatService).

CreateProjectRequest.description:
Request body for creating a project.

Accepts every field UpdateProjectRequest does, bar `id` and `archived`.
A field settable only on update leaves a freshly created project at its
default until a separate PUT the create form has no way to make: the
daemon's flow-score category_fit silently could not match work to a new
project until `category` was added here, and a GitHub repo, autostart
path or goal type typed at creation was dropped the same way.
CreateProjectRequest.title: CreateProjectRequest

LedgerAdjustment.description:
A balance adjustment as its ledger week shows it: the record, and
`applied`, the hours it actually moved the balance — `hours` for a

LedgerTotals.description:
The balance as of today and the three terms that move it, since the

adjusted" lines and the ledger's foot. The opening balance is the
contract's own. `worked` is the hours the balance counts: through
`ended_on`, under a term that owes hours. Hours worked under an
objective or 0-hour term are in the weeks' `worked` and not here.
LedgerTotals.title: LedgerTotals

LedgerWeek.description:
One week of the ledger. See `domain/ledger.py` for what each figure is
and when it is None.
LedgerWeek.title: LedgerWeek

LinkedIdentityInfo.description: An identity at a provider that signs into this account.
LinkedIdentityInfo.title: LinkedIdentityInfo

`contract` is the domain model as stored — the terms, region, opening

/api/billing/report-links`. Every key is required, null where it may be.

That the projects are billed to the client, and that the range is over,
read other records and the clock: they are checked where a link is made
(`ReportLinkService`), since a stored link is re-validated on every read
and must not become unreadable when a project moves or a day passes.

UpdateBeatRequest.title: UpdateBeatRequest

UpdateProjectRequest.description:
Request body for updating a project.

Only `id` and `name` are required, and every other field is read by
presence (`model_fields_set`): left out, the stored value is kept; sent,
it replaces it. A client sends what it edits, and must not wipe what it
does not know: the project page's colour picker sends no GitHub repo,
category or autostart repos, and while "not sent" read as "clear" every
colour change reset all three. The defaults below are therefore never
written over a stored value.

`null` clears `description`, `color`, `weekly_goal`, `github_repo`,
`category` and `contract`; `[]` clears `autostart_repos`. `archived` and
`goal_type` have no empty state and refuse null (422); `kind` has none
either, and reads null as left out. A day job moved to another kind
loses its contract with it; a contract sent with any other kind is a 409.
UpdateProjectRequest.title: UpdateProjectRequest

VacationEntitlement.description:
The vacation days a day job gives, counted the way the arithmetic
counts a day off: for a five-day week (decision 3), so a week off is
five days whatever the percentage, and a 4-day week with 20 days is
entered as 25.

Counting starts on `opening_on`, with `opening_days` left for the rest
of that calendar year (carry-over included, negative when overdrawn) —
the figure off the contract or an HR statement. Nothing before it is
reconstructed: a contract the migration started at the first beat,
years back, must not be credited years of leave nobody recorded.

Every figure is a whole or half day. The rules are field constraints,
so a 422 names the leaf. The one rule tying the entitlement to the rest
of the contract — `opening_on` inside its dates — is checked where a
contract is written (`ProjectService`), for the reason the region is:
this model is re-validated on every read, and a stored entitlement can
be paired with new terms by the keep-unsent merge.
VacationEntitlement.title: VacationEntitlement

VacationYear.description:
`GET /{id}/vacation`: one calendar year of a day job's vacation
entitlement, in days, every figure a whole or half day. See
`domain/vacation.py` for how each is worked out. Only what the client
cannot derive: the days per year, the opening and the end date are on
the contract it already holds.
VacationYear.title: VacationYear

Export everything a balance and a bill are made of, as JSON for
backup: the projects (contract included), the sessions, the absences and
the balance adjustments; the clients, each project's billing, the
entries marked billable or not, and the billing budgets.

post.description:
Import a full JSON backup, version 1.0 to 1.3, into the caller's
account. Safe to re-import: projects, beats and clients are written by
id, a project's billing replaces the one on its project, a billing
budget the one on its scope and an override the one on its beat, and an
absence or an adjustment replaces the one on its project and date, as
its own route does. Nothing is deleted: the account's own budgets
survive a file without them.

The whole file is checked first, and a file that fails writes nothing:

- a malformed record, a project's, a session's or a client's id
  included, is a 422 that names it;
- a file holding a project, a session or a client whose id is another
  account's is a 409 `BACKUP_OF_ANOTHER_ACCOUNT`;
- a billing whose project or client, an override whose session, or a
  billing budget whose client or project is in neither the file nor the
  account is a 422 that names it;
- a client, a billing or a billing budget that its route would refuse,
  against the file over the account (a currency the API does not know,
  or one changed once priced or under a money budget; billing on a
  project that is not freelance, or a billed project moved away from
  freelance; billing moved to a client in another currency; a budget on
  a project billed nowhere), is that route's error, its detail naming
  the record. The retroactive gate is not applied: a restore puts back
  what was.

Clients are written first, then projects as a project write is: the
contract's checks, and the reconcile against the contract it replaces.
A refusal there is that write's error and stops the import, with no
transaction: the clients and the projects before it in the file stay
written, and nothing after them is. Then each project's billing, the
billing budgets, the beats and the overrides. Absences and adjustments go last, through their
own routes' rules, against the projects as restored, and one those rules
refuse (an absence on a project that is no longer a day job; an
adjustment outside the contract's first day through today in `tz`) is
left out and listed under `skipped` with the code its route would
answer. Billing, budgets included, is never skipped: its rules ran
before the first write.

get.description:
One calendar year of a day job's vacation entitlement, in days: what
the year gives (`accrued`, pro-rated in the year the contract ends; null
in the opening year, whose figure is the opening's), what the year
before carried in, what is available, what is booked (the `vacation`
days, past and planned, on weekdays inside the contract's dates that are
not its holidays) and what remains. Every figure is a whole or half day.
409 on a project that is not a day job (NOT_A_DAY_JOB), without a
contract (NO_CONTRACT) or an entitlement (NO_VACATION_ENTITLEMENT), and
for a year before the opening's or after the contract's end
(VACATION_YEAR_OUT_OF_RANGE).

parameters.description: Defaults to the current year in `tz`.

get.description:
List flow windows for the current user within a date range.

Optional filters narrow the result, AND-composed:
- `project_id` — only windows captured while a timer was running on
  this project (i.e. `active_project_id` matches).
- `editor_repo` — only windows whose VS Code heartbeat reported this
  workspace path. Use the absolute path the daemon stores; the
  companion / web UI render a shortened display form on top.
- `editor_language` — only windows whose VS Code heartbeat reported
  this language id (e.g. "go", "typescriptreact").
- `bundle_id` — only windows whose dominant frontmost app matched
  this macOS bundle id (e.g. "com.microsoft.VSCode").

Return drift events recorded since `since` (defaults to last 30 min).

Drift events are stored as flow windows with `dominant_category="drift"`
by the daemon's `shield` package. This endpoint is the companion-side
read surface — the daemon already fires a native macOS notification
on the desktop, so the companion poller adds the same prompt for users
on iOS / Android / desktops without the daemon installed.

post.description:
Check if a timer should be auto-started based on flow state.

Called by the daemon when Flow Score >= 0.7 for 8+ consecutive minutes.

Matching priority:
1. editor_repo against project.autostart_repos — if the user's
   editor heartbeat carries a workspace path that one project
   claims as its autostart_repo, that's the most-specific match.
   Disambiguates two coding projects with the same category.
2. dominant_category against project.category — fallback when
   the editor_repo is empty (no editor active) or no project
   claims it.

On a positive match the suggestion is also persisted via
`pending_repo.create` so the companion's notification poller can
pick it up via `GET /api/signals/pending-suggestions` and fire
`notifyAutoTimerSuggestion` for users whose desktop daemon isn't
the OS notifier (mobile, headless servers, etc.).

Previously only matched by category, so two same-category
projects couldn't be disambiguated and the docstring's mention
of autostart_repos didn't reflect the implementation.
